Today, Apple announced an update to Final Cut Camera, along with updated versions of Pages, Keynote, Numbers, Pixelmator Pro, and Freeform. Below is a summary of the new features.

Apple rolls out an update to its "Creator Studio" app, but some new features are available to non-subscribers as well

Apple today announced a range of new features for its popular iWork suite—Pages, Keynote, and Numbers—along with improvements to Pixelmator Pro and Freeform.

Some of the new features are exclusive to Apple Creator Studio, but select features will be available to all users. Below is a roundup of all the new features, based on the Apple Newsroom:

Pages, Keynote, Numbers

Apple says the update lets users ask Siri questions about Pages, Keynote, or Numbers and get answers. It's not yet clear whether this requires Siri AI, but it's a strong possibility. The update also adds the ability to "request access to a shared presentation, document, or spreadsheet," making collaboration easier because the file owner no longer has to enable sharing themselves.

Pages for Mac gets a "Screen View" mode that "optimizes content for reading and focused writing," while Numbers gains "trigonometric, statistical, and logical functions" to help users tackle complex problems in spreadsheets.

In addition, Apple Creator Studio subscribers get access to new templates and themes across all three iWork apps. Keynote will also add a smart slide-generation feature that automatically creates images to match the theme of the presentation.

Pixelmator Pro

Pixelmator Pro for iPad adds the "Select and Mask" tool, previously available only on Mac. Both Mac and iPad versions also gain two new template collections geared toward sports and dynamic themes, as well as templates designed for "launching new ideas, businesses, or products."

Top Liked Comment by Richard Lewis (Rich)

You may be wondering whether the standalone Pixelmator Pro app has been updated? The answer is no (not yet). The current version, 3.8, hasn't been updated in roughly five months.

The app also adds a Podcasts category, making it easier to create cover art that meets the size requirements of major podcast platforms.

Freeform
